mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 3.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 3.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 4.0% for three consecutive months signals weakening labor demand, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 4.0% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST over two consecutive quarters indicates deteriorating aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in INDPRO above its 12-month moving average by more than 2% for three consecutive months signals improving supply conditions, which boosts corporate margins and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-mo MA +2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average by >2% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in FEDFUNDS below 1.5% coincident with a rise in CPIAUCSL above 3% signals a policy lag response to inflation, which typically precedes a short-term equity rally as markets anticipate easing, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS drops below 1.5% AND CPIAUCSL rises above 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS < 1.5% and CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average by more than 0.5% in a single month signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS jumps above its 12-month moving average by >0.5% in a single month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both GDPC1 and RSAFS over two consecutive months signals strengthening aggregate demand and corporate liquidity, which supports higher earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both rise for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and RSAFS rise for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent fall in INDPRO below its 6-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a broad-based supply contraction, which increases input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 6-mo MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO is below its 6-month moving average for four consecutive months.
